candidateDecisions.label: U.S. Politics, Identity and Global Affairs
Hemispheric migration, political economy and regional change
candidateDecisions.assessment: UCR supports comparative empire, migration, identity, environmental justice and political economy through individual courses. The active curriculum does not sustain a dedicated Canada and Latin America sequence or a coherent additional hemispheric plan distinct from the selected directions.

analysis: The broad plan connects Native American and gender histories, American media and race, comparative politics, and historical inquiry to broader social and cultural context. The media and culture plan builds from narrative and film to media technologies, adaptation, creative work and documentary, with an American anchor in media, race and gender history. The politics plan centers on comparative institutions, empire, international relations and law, rights and conflict, with the U.S. anchor supplied by historical study and the media courses. Introductory courses precede qualifying and advanced work in all three. The case distinguishes a substantive point of overlap from a complementary course. The six aligned rows support concrete common domains or methods. General economics, literary study and creative production do not carry a designated comparator match. Comparable work in migration, inequality and political economy does not supply sustained Canada and Latin America coursework, and recycling that material would not create a distinct fourth plan.

alignment.rationale: Groningen continues its dedicated Americas survey. UCR’s Modern History provides wider historical context.

Groningen studies political and media theory together. UCR studies contemporary social theory and media in separate courses.
Both guide students through a sustained research project. The UCR course focuses on historical inquiry and source criticism.
Groningen examines how stories shape identities. UCR offers related literary and media analysis.
Groningen compares societies and cultures across the Americas. UCR offers related work in history, politics and literary interpretation.
Choose a faculty-wide course in one of the published themes.
Both develop written and spoken argument. UCR emphasizes rhetoric and audience.
This course continues Groningen’s introduction to cultural theory.
Groningen introduces cultural analysis of race, class and gender. UCR explores these themes through sociology and history.
Both develop independent research through question design and analysis. UCR focuses on qualitative social research.
